newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Caller threatens to bomb Japan's Jakarta mission.
newsitem.headline: Caller threatens to bomb Japan's Jakarta mission.

text.p: Japan's embassy in Jakarta was evacuated on Wednesday morning after an anonymous phone caller threatened to bomb the building but no explosives were found, police and officials said.
Police said the bomb squad searched the embassy but nothing was found.
"Someone made a phone call at 8:25 a.m. (0125 GMT) to the office saying they were going to bomb our embassy in an hour," said an embassy official, who asked not to be named.
He said embassy staff, including ambassador Taizo Watanabe, had moved to the information centre next to the main building while it was searched.
Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokesman Ghaffar Fadyl said an unidentified man had called the embassy. "He just said there is a bomb somewhere there and just hung up," he said.
"It was nothing but a hoax," he said.
The threat followed reports in the local press that the military had arrested four men on Tuesday morning it suspected were planning to set off an explosion at a shopping mall in North Jakarta.

"The four are believed to belong to a group which always tries to cause trouble in the capital, with the ultimate goal of disrupting the general elections," Jakarta military commander Major-General Sutiyoso was quoted as telling the Jakarta Post newspaper.
Military officers could not be reached for comment.
Official sources said there had been a couple of other bomb warnings on Tuesday in Jakarta but nothing had come of them.
Nearly 125 million Indonesians are eligible to vote in national and local elections on Thursday which are held every five years.
The 27-day election campaign which ended last Friday experienced some of the worst political violence under President Suharto's 30-year rule.
The Jakarta Post newspaper said officers became suspicious after the four men arrested in North Jakarta were seen wandering around the Kelapa Gading shopping centre early on Tuesday.
It said the officers later confiscated stones and gasoline from the men, but did not find any bombs.
